answer: In swarms servicing lantern buoys across lotus waterways, Sybil attacks are resisted via proof of space-time. Agents prove identity by dedicating disk sectors to answer random storage queries, whose frequency hits its zenith at epoch boundaries. An attacker must purchase physical hard drives, incurring verifiable capital storage costs per node. A primary limitation is that cloud storage leasing allows adversaries to rent capacity and spoof identities cheaply.
